title: A sweet tea or coffee named in Serbian, or an Ice Tea, is never saved as 0
why: Coach Milan 22 November 2026, 21:11 to 21:12, after DT336 was built (0.3.174): the words that block the 0 miss Serbian word forms and Ice Tea; yes, clean this one before the next ticket. 21:12: a sweet tea with a zero calorie sweetener gets the heads-up; its pack prints a table, so the values are typed from it and it saves as 0 like zero cola.

opportunity.from: Claude's own look while building DT336, 22 November 2026.
opportunity.job: Scan a sweet tea or a coffee with milk and get its real values.
opportunity.kind: A wrong result: a sweet drink with no values in the database is saved as 0.
opportunity.why_now: 0.3.174 brought the 0. A wrong 0 is saved with no question, and nobody sees it.

problem: The words that block the 0 are matched as whole words, in the one form they are written. Serbian changes the end of a word: sa šećerom, bez šećera, sa mlekom, s ukusom breskve. None of them is šećer, mleko or ukus, so Čaj sa šećerom and Kafa sa mlekom count as 0 when the product database has no category and no values. The block words have no Cyrillic form at all, so Чај са шећером counts as 0 too. Ice Tea, written without the d, is not a block word, so Ice Tea Peach counts as 0.
story: When I scan a sweet tea or a coffee with milk, I want to type its values from the pack, so that my day does not count it as 0.
now: Čaj sa šećerom, scanned by its barcode, with a name and no category and no values in the database: the label check says Tea has almost no calories, so it is saved as 0 kcal. Confirm & save saves it with 0 kcal and 0 protein, and its card says No PD: it has 0 kcal.
proposed: The Serbian words that block the 0 are matched by how the word starts, in Latin and Cyrillic, so šećer also blocks šećera, šećerom and šećerni. The Serbian words for the other block words are added: sirup, krem, pavlaka, šlag, čips, sirće, torta, orasi, ukus. Ice Tea and Icetea block the 0 too. A product they block gets the amber heads-up of DT336 AC7. The list of what counts as 0 stays as it is.
looked_at: Matching the Serbian forms of tea, coffee and water too: not chosen, a product name says Čaj or Kafa as it is, and a missed 0 only costs a heads-up. Asking whether a sweet tea has sugar: not chosen, the pack of a sweetened tea prints a table, so the values are typed from it.
checks: Area plus the German sweep (with B158): 21 of 21 walkthroughs passed (docs/qa/runs/0.3.175.json).
decision: Go, Coach Milan 22 November 2026, 21:57, built with B158. Built in 0.3.175.

ac.title: A Serbian form blocks the 0
ac.text: Given I scan Čaj sa šećerom whose database entry has a name, no category and no values, when the label check opens, then it gets the amber heads-up of DT336 AC7, the values are empty and the box I checked the values is there

ac.title: In Cyrillic, and the other Serbian words
ac.text: Given the name is Чај са шећером, Kafa sa mlekom or Čaj s ukusom breskve, with no category and no values, when the label check opens, then it gets the heads-up, never 0

ac.title: Ice Tea
ac.text: Given I scan Ice Tea Peach with no category and no values, when the label check opens, then it gets the heads-up, never 0

ac.title: A sugar free tea
ac.text: Given I scan Čaj bez šećera with no category and no values, when the label check opens, then it gets the heads-up, and the values I type from the pack are saved as typed, 0 included

ac.title: A plain tea is as in 0.3.174
ac.text: Given I scan Čaj od nane with no category and no values, when the label check opens, then one line says Tea has almost no calories, so it is saved as 0 kcal, as today

details: The pictures are the real app on one scratch build of main, not committed. The database's answer is given in place of it.

A Serbian block word matches every word that starts with it: šećer, mlek, mleč, čokolad, kolač, keks, sok, sirup, krem, pavlak, šlag, čips, sirć, tort, orah, oras, ukus, and leden before čaj. The same in Cyrillic.
short: Serbian word forms and Ice Tea block the 0
